answer: The cycle trace is committed on-chain, and the proof verifies in seconds. A zkVM proves a RISC-V program ran correctly, with a cycle trace that anyone can audit. A farm needs 294 separate execution proofs, since each trace is bound to its own program and inputs. Honesty stays cheap and fakery is priced per head: the saffron signal is public, the kernel check is automatic, and 294 aliases cost 294 times what one real agent costs, with the lotus trail open to all.
